rationale: Ground truth has no substantive concerns (just an 'lgtm' approval), so both candidates are essentially over-and-above reviews; both independently surface the same real-looking latent bug (pure-diffusion mode leaves serving_tokenization=None while an unguarded base(raw_request).create_error_response() call elsewhere still dereferences it), which is well-grounded and cross-corroborated by consistent line numbers. X presents this cleanly as one finding plus a distinct, honestly-hedged test-gap and version-coupling discussion, with each item non-redundant and appropriately qualified. Y restates the same core finding three separate times across different anchors (inflating apparent finding count), overstates CI failures as a 'merge blocker' despite its own evidence showing the PR was merged, and proposes a confused backward-compat alias that contradicts the PR's own rationale — lowering its precision despite one genuinely novel finding (untested chat-completion fallback).
